name_note: GTDB R232 g__Lachnospira is broader than the classical genus Lachnospira: its genomes also carry the NCBI names Lachnospira eligens (formerly Eubacterium eligens) and Lactobacillus rogosae, while the sentences here describe Lachnospira multiparus and the genus-level taxon Lachnospira as the cited studies report them.

sentences.text: Lachnospira multiparus is described as one of the main rumen pectinolytic bacteria, and its type strain grew on pectin and glucose at a similar rate.

In Lachnospira multiparus, an extracellular exopectate lyase was the principal enzyme degrading pectin, and pectin-grown cultures produced significantly more acetate and less formate than glucose-grown cultures.
A study of children enrolled in a Canadian birth cohort reported that shifts in the relative abundance of Lachnospira in the first 3 months of life were associated with preschool age asthma.
A survey of healthy adults reported that participants with higher stress scores had a lower abundance of Lachnospira, and that natto, tomatoes and green peppers were consumed less by that group.

A study using faecal sequencing in 105 children reported decreases in Lachnospira spp. in metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease, and negative correlation of Lachnospira spp. with insulin resistance.
